priceModel.meaning: A price sensitivity grid. Alpha = 0.50/0.75/1.00 is an explicit convenience assumption, not a fitted distribution. Historical retention ratios and the current provisional ratio are separate stress assumptions.

backtest.testedModel: Undiscounted historical analogue returns; geometric mean across available analogues, compared with unchanged current price.
limits: Only two retrospectively selected post-decline cutoffs; no significance test or predictive-probability claim.
The 90/180/365-day horizons share the same two regimes and are not six independent trials.
Past reference cycle extrema are selected retrospectively, although each selection window was completed before its replay cutoff.
Current low candidates are computed from each cutoff prefix, not replaced by later-known lows.
No outcome from 2025 onward enters the default evaluation. The current cycle is not used as a validation example.

methodology.observationTime: UTC daily observation label, not intraday high/low
methodology.analogueFormula: S_j(h) = P_t × P_(b_j + d + h) / P_(b_j + d), d = t − b_current
methodology.analogueMeaning: Replays realized historical returns at the same number of days after each past low; no least-squares curve fit or time warp is used.
methodology.calendarFormula: calendar(event, extraMonths) = observedEventDate + (48 − extraMonths) calendar months
methodology.interpolationFormula: log P(t) = (1 − w) log A + w log B, w = elapsedDays / intervalDays
methodology.interpolationMeaning: Only a visual connection between specified assumptions. Interior dates do not have daily-return predictive meaning.
methodology.reversalRule: The initial trend must first move at least 20%. Then an interior high requires a later decline of at least 20%, and an interior low requires a later rebound of at least 20%, within that borrowed historical path. The initial and terminal unconfirmed extrema are omitted.
methodology.highZoneRule: First daily observation at or above the chosen fraction of the subsequently observed peak; definition is retrospective and changes if the peak changes.
methodology.noDoubleCompression: The bottom-holds model already uses the earlier current low; it receives no additional month subtraction. Extra 3/4/5 months applies only to the separate 48-month calendar scenarios.
methodology.dateWindows: Min/max of named historical intervals or explicit arithmetic sensitivities, never confidence intervals.
methodology.priceBands: Min/max of named assumption combinations, never a probability distribution.
methodology.missingDays: A reference path with any missing UTC day is excluded; missing prices are not synthesized.

warnings: Conditional historical scenarios do not mathematically prove a future peak, trough, price, or 4-year law. Any finite observed history admits future continuations with a higher high or lower low.
The current peak and low are provisional; a lower low invalidates the bottom-aligned paths and revises all dependent dates.
Only three historical cycle references exist. Daily rows, parameter variants, and closely spaced horizons do not increase the number of independent cycles.

An observed high-zone entry is not an absolute peak. Consistent first-entry definitions can produce different results in the 2021 double-top cycle; an apparent 3–5-month advance is not a fitted acceleration constant.
The historical-analogue envelope is a descriptive range of three selected histories. Actual outcomes can lie outside it.
Internal peak/trough markers belong to the historical analogue, with its own subsequent 20% reversal. Unconfirmed right-edge extremes are not labeled turning points.
The macro path and its price band are schematic sensitivities. The representative alpha and retention ratio are convenient display assumptions, not expected returns or estimates of likelihood.
The 48-month baseline inherits the observed current event dates. Subtracting the prior early arrival again would count the same shift twice.
The default historical replay stops before 2025, checks at most 365 days, and does not validate the 730-day path or 2029/2030 macro scenarios.
